title: SENNIAF abuse-accountability protest, second consecutive day
location: Outside SENNIAF headquarters, Bella Vista, Panama City
scope: A local gathering at the national child-protection agency; reporting places it on the second consecutive day of protests, but continuity and boundaries across days remain unresolved.
threshold_50_evidence: La Prensa S004 describes hundreds of people at the gathering on the previous afternoon (2021-02-16). This supports the 50-person threshold but gives no exact or bounded count.

start_date.summary: La Prensa's 17 February report dates the gathering to the previous afternoon; TVN calls the 16 February action the second consecutive day of protests.

location.summary: Both reports place the demonstration outside SENNIAF in Bella Vista, Panama City.

demands.summary: Protesters demanded action and justice concerning alleged abuse of children in shelters, addressing SENNIAF, MIDES and the Presidency.

participants_original.summary: La Prensa uses the qualitative phrase 'cientos de personas'; no exact total or range is supplied.

state_response.summary: TVN reports police were present and watched without describing an event-specific intervention. The local May 2015 codebook includes state inaction under ignore; this is a provisional coding interpretation for review.

notes: The phrase 'hundreds' supports the size threshold, but no numeric estimate is assigned. Reported tire burning is not attributed to protesters, so protester violence remains unknown. The same grievance recurs on neighboring dates; this candidate is not automatically merged with those daily reports. The ignore response is provisional: TVN reports police watching, and the May 2015 manual treats state inaction as ignore; review against the current official procedure.
open_questions: Was this a distinct one-day gathering or part of one continuous action spanning consecutive days?
Can another body source establish a precise attendance estimate, organizer, or physical ending?
Who, if anyone, set tires alight, and what other event-specific state responses occurred?

title: SENNIAF abuse-accountability protest, third consecutive day
location: Outside SENNIAF headquarters, Bella Vista, Panama City
scope: A local gathering outside SENNIAF; students later left the area toward the University of Panama. No protest at the destination is established by this report.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending: the article reports university students but no protester count or description establishing 50 or more participants.

start_date.summary: La Prensa dates the report to 17 February and calls this the third consecutive day of protests outside SENNIAF.

end_date.summary: The report says the group withdrew from SENNIAF at about 5:45 p.m.; students then left the area toward the University of Panama. No continuation at the university is reported.

location.summary: The gathering and police response occurred outside the SENNIAF headquarters in Panama City.

demands.summary: Protesters demanded justice for abuse at shelters, names of responsible shelter staff, and answers about funding; the article also reports a demand to dismiss the MIDES minister and SENNIAF officials.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Police crowd-control officers used pepper spray on demonstrators.

notes: The report documents pepper spray and says the protest occurred on the third consecutive day. It reports an attempt to topple security barriers but does not establish that barriers were brought down; protester violence remains unknown pending review. The president's public statement and instructions are not coded as accommodation because the report does not describe a meeting or an agreement to take up the protesters' demands. The removal demand's category may warrant review; political_behavior_process is used provisionally.
open_questions: Does any source establish a crowd of at least 50 on 17 February?
Should the reported attempt to topple security barriers be coded as protester violence under the manual?
Does the explicit removal demand also meet the manual's removal_of_politician category?
Did protest activity continue at the University of Panama or elsewhere after the group left SENNIAF?
Is the 17 February gathering separate from, or continuous with, the protests on adjacent days?

title: SENNIAF gathering monitored by the Defensoría
scope: A protest gathering noted by the national ombudsman's monitoring page; total turnout, demands and relation to earlier days remain unknown.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending: the monitoring passage gives no total attendance. It notes that a small group remained at 6:30 p.m., but this does not establish total turnout earlier in the day.

start_date.summary: The Defensoría's monitoring entry concerns protest activity at SENNIAF on 19 February 2021.

location.summary: The monitoring entry identifies SENNIAF as the location.

state_response.arrests.summary: The Defensoría reported three people detained: two Panamanian adults and one Nicaraguan.

participants_original.summary: The monitor left at 6:30 p.m. with a small group remaining; no total turnout is provided.

notes: This contemporaneous monitor establishes protest activity and three detentions but not a 50-person turnout or a specific demand in the consulted passage. The Defensoría's note that it was then looking for a missing protester is contemporaneous information, not a present-day status claim. The relationship to the protests on 16–17 February is not established.
open_questions: What demand was made at this gathering, and was it directed to the Panamanian state?
Were the three detainees released or charged, and did any other state response occur?
Was this a distinct gathering or part of a continuous/repeated SENNIAF protest episode?
